supporting_observations.claim: At 13:41 UTC, maria.lopez ran PowerShell from her interactive session to compress \\FILE-HD-01\Shared\Clients into C:\Users\maria.lopez\AppData\Local\Temp\c.zip; Sysmon recorded creation of that archive.
At 13:45 UTC, maria.lopez's Chrome process was launched to open sendbox-files.io, a file-sharing destination not listed as approved.

At 13:48 UTC, the proxy recorded approximately 51 MB of client-to-server bytes in a successful CONNECT tunnel to sendbox-files.io, and endpoint records associate the proxy connection with Chrome running as maria.lopez.

The sequence of creating an archive from the Clients share, then transferring tens of MB through the user's browser to an unapproved file-sharing destination, strongly supports likely data exfiltration and makes a malicious disposition appropriate.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy and Zeek records show a CONNECT tunnel and byte counts, but the provided records do not expose the encrypted tunnel's uploaded payload or identify the specific file transferred (T019-00170, T019-00171).

The available endpoint and network records do not directly link c.zip to the 51 MB transfer; that connection is inferred from the sequence and context (T019-00117, T019-00119, T019-00170, T019-00171).
claims_not_established: The exact contents of c.zip or whether the 51 MB transfer contained that archive.
Whether the destination accepted, retained, or made the transferred data available; the CONNECT status alone does not establish application-level upload completion.
Whether maria.lopez personally initiated the activity or had authorization for this transfer.
additional_evidence_needed: Preserve and examine c.zip, including its hash, contents, timestamps, and any remaining endpoint or browser artifacts.
Review FILE-HD-01 share and file-access auditing around the archive creation to identify what was read and by which account.
Obtain proxy TLS-inspection, DLP, or destination-side records, if available, to determine the uploaded content and upload outcome.
Validate with maria.lopez and the data owner whether the archive and transfer were authorized; preserve relevant endpoint and account evidence.
unrelated_findings: A dotnet-sdk-installer.exe ran from maria.lopez's Temp directory with quiet-install arguments after the alerted transfer. Review separately; the provided records do not establish whether it was authorized or malicious (T019-00181, T019-00182, T019-00210, T019-00211).
